key_insight: In pediatric first-onset nephrotic syndrome, pretreatment anti-nephrin antibody levels distinguished clinical phenotypes: standard-range positivity was associated with steroid sensitivity, while high titers were enriched in steroid resistance.
clinical_relevance: The assay may support future disease classification and prediction of steroid response in pediatric nephrotic syndrome; this is not an AI or cancer drug discovery study.
method: Developed an automated immunoassay using a modified recombinant nephrin antigen.
Evaluated antibody titers in a prospective Japanese pediatric discovery cohort and an independent validation cohort.
Checked assay findings using immunoprecipitation–Western blotting, kidney-tissue colocalization, and antigen inhibition.
evidence_signal: In the discovery cohort (n=103), antibodies were detected in 83/83 steroid-sensitive and 9/16 steroid-resistant cases; an independent cohort (n=42) showed similar phenotype associations.
watch_item: Small phenotype subgroups and the Japanese pediatric setting limit generalizability; broader validation is needed before routine clinical use.
paper_title: Establishment of an Anti-Nephrin Autoantibody Assay and the Predictive and Diagnostic Significance of Pre-treatment Antibody Titers in Pediatric Nephrotic Syndrome
